FINDING_ID: CONFIRM C0001
SEVERITY: 0.91
FLAW_CLASS: 1
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.1
DESCRIPTION: FIND: _compute_rho() has an off-by-one error in earliest-round gating. `len(raw_counts)` corresponds exactly to the 1-based round index (since one count is added per round), so `round_idx` should be exactly `len(raw_counts)` without subtracting 1.
FOLLOW: Without this fix, the gate `round_idx >= cfg.rho_earliest_round` evaluates false for exactly 1 round longer than configured, artificially delaying convergence by 1 round. Downstream convergence signals are corrupted.
ANALYSE: CONFIRMED. The logic mathematically forces an artificial 1-round delay against the configured earliest stop.
PROPOSED_FIX: 
<<<< SEARCH bench/reference_runner.py
    round_idx = len(raw_counts) - 1
    churn = rho_avg < cfg.rho_threshold and round_idx >= cfg.rho_earliest_round
====
    round_idx = len(raw_counts)
    churn = rho_avg < cfg.rho_threshold and round_idx >= cfg.rho_earliest_round
>>>> REPLACE
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: CONFIRM C0010
SEVERITY: 0.85
FLAW_CLASS: 1
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.1
DESCRIPTION: FIND: `_compute_rho` aborts immediately if the current round yields 0 raw findings via `if not raw_counts or raw_counts[-1] == 0:`.
FOLLOW: Returning early causes `churn = False` to be returned. This actively blocks termination on rounds with zero findings, which is exactly when discovery efficiency is at its absolute lowest (0) and convergence SHOULD be triggered.
ANALYSE: CONFIRMED. Early exit completely bypasses the rolling window churn detection when it is needed most. Division by zero is already protected by the ternary operator below.
PROPOSED_FIX: 
<<<< SEARCH bench/reference_runner.py
    if not raw_counts or raw_counts[-1] == 0:
        return 0.0, 0.0, False
====
    if not raw_counts:
        return 0.0, 0.0, False
>>>> REPLACE
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: CONFIRM C0008
SEVERITY: 0.75
FLAW_CLASS: 1
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.1
DESCRIPTION: FIND: `contested_count` logic gap hardcodes `current_round - oldest > 1` (equivalent to `>= 2`), completely ignoring the configurable `grace_period` parameter.
FOLLOW: A custom configuration setting `grace_period = 3` would still calculate the contestation threshold as 2 rounds, breaking orchestrator tuning.
ANALYSE: CONFIRMED. Replacing the hardcoded scalar with the parameterized threshold restores configuration control.
PROPOSED_FIX: 
<<<< SEARCH bench/reference_runner.py
            if unresolved:
                oldest = min(v["round"] for v in unresolved)
                if current_round - oldest > 1:
                    count += 1
====
            if unresolved:
                oldest = min(v["round"] for v in unresolved)
                if current_round - oldest >= grace_period:
                    count += 1
>>>> REPLACE
VERIFIED: TRUE
